rule: No map in this corpus may be used to adjudicate a present-day ancestry, descent or identity claim.
rationale: A historical map is evidence about the people who made it. Treating it as a verdict on who anyone is today is a category error that this trench exists to describe rather than commit.

rule: A reception artefact is evidence about its own moment and its makers, never about antiquity.
rationale: The 1930s map tells you about the 1930s. Reading it as testimony about the second century is the exact move the reception it documents was making.

rule: An item whose creator or source is unidentified may only hold the reference_artefact role.
rationale: Apparent detail is not provenance. An unsourced map that looks authoritative is the most dangerous kind, and the role is what stops the interface presenting it as evidence.

rule: No artefact is shown until its rights are cleared; description is the fallback and is sufficient.
rationale: The essay's argument does not depend on reproducing any particular sheet, and saying what a map does is usually clearer than showing it.

rule: Classification precedes use, and a class that stays class_only may not enter the production corpus.
rationale: A class is a real finding and an unselected item is not a source. Freezing the distinction stops an interaction being built on artefacts nobody has chosen.
